title: Annotated screenshot is the whole specification
tests: Vision plus intent. The ticket text says nothing about what to change: the entire request is a crude MS Paint annotation on a screenshot, an arrow and the handwritten words 'Remove the save option' pointing at a control. The model must work out what is being asked for, not just transcribe what it sees, and must not mistake the annotation for part of the app or invent a defect.
request: Analyse this ticket. What exactly is being asked for, and is it ready to build?

tickets.summary: Login screen change requested by the client
description: The client sent this through after the demo. They have marked up the screenshot with what they want changed.
Attaching it as-is. Can someone pick this up for the next sprint?

answer_key.expect: The request is to remove the "Save" control (the save-username toggle beside the user name field) from the mobile Online Banking login screen.

The request exists only as an annotation drawn on the screenshot: the handwritten words "Remove the save option" and a thick arrow pointing up at that control, added in an image editor rather than being part of the app.
The screen is the "Enter your Online Banking credentials" login screen, showing user name TESTRELAXLUX4 with the password field empty.
Removing the save option will affect customers who have already saved their user name, so a decision is needed about what happens to them; the ticket says nothing about it.
The ticket has no written requirement in text, no acceptance criteria, no estimate and no assignee, and gives no reason for the change.
It is not ready to build: the whole specification is a drawing on an image, and it needs to be written up and confirmed first.
Next actions: confirm the exact control and the reason with the client (via Aroha Walker), write the requirement and acceptance criteria into the ticket, then estimate and assign it.
Describes this as a bug, error or failure, for example claiming the screenshot shows an error message or that login is broken.
answer_key.claim: The screenshot shows an error on the login screen, and the customer is unable to log in.

answer_key.expect: Treats the drawn arrow or the handwritten words as part of the application's interface, or claims the app itself displays that wording.
answer_key.claim: The login screen displays the text "Remove the save option" next to an arrow icon, which should be removed from the app.
